items.actClause:
AN ACT requiring the division of veterans' services to review issues relating
to veterans' abilities to access state parks, lands and facilities; and
providing for the repeal of such provisions upon expiration thereof
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6706

SPONSOR: BENJAMIN
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act requiring the division of veterans' services to
review issues relating to veterans' abilities to access state parks,
lands and facilities; and providing for the repeal of such provisions
upon expiration thereof

 
PURPOSE:

Requires the New York State Division of Veterans' Service in consulta-
tion with the Office of Parks, Recreation and Historic Preservation, the
Department of Environmental Conservation, the Department of Health and
the Office of Mental Health to review issues relating to veteran' abili-
ties to access state parks, lands and facilities.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Nature has been used for health improvement for centuries, including
during World War I and World War II when service members participated in
"horticultural therapy" which included working in gardens to address
mental exhaustion and improve functioning of injured limits. Recent
studies have found that time outdoors can be valuable adjunct therapy in
addition to more tradition types of health care.  Outdoor-based thera-
peutic programs hold promise for people suffering with Post-Traumatic
Stress Disorder (PTSD) and Substance Use Disorder.

The "Outdoor Rx Act" will be the first step in the progress of how the
State of New York can better address the needs of those veterans who are
trying to readjust back to the civilian life by being outside.

 
EXISTING LAW:

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Nature has been used for health improvement for centuries, including
during World War I and World War II when service members participated in
"horticultural therapy" which included working in gardens to address
mental exhaustion and improve functioning of injured limits. Recent
studies have found that time outdoors can be valuable adjunct therapy in
addition to more tradition types of health care. Outdoor-based therapeu-
tic programs hold promise for people suffering with Post-Traumatic
Stress Disorder (PTSD) and Substance Use Disorder.

The "Outdoor Rx Act" will be the first step in the progress of how the
State of New York can better address the needs of those veterans who are
trying to readjust back to the civilian life by being outside.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New Bill

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None

 
LOCAL FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None
 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately and shall expire and be deemed
repealed December 31, 2021.
